skill.name: functional-patterns
skill.description: Functional programming guidance for TypeScript services, including pure functions, immutability, composition, Result, Option, and dependency injection patterns.
skill.summary: Apply practical functional patterns to make TypeScript services easier to test and maintain.
skill.author: DoubleslashSE

content.value_statement: Mutable logic and hidden side effects make Node.js services hard to test. This skill shows functional patterns for predictable TypeScript design.
actual_capabilities: Explains pure functions and the pure core, impure shell pattern.
Shows immutable object and array update techniques for TypeScript.
Demonstrates function composition, pipe helpers, and higher-order functions.
Defines Result and Option patterns for typed errors and missing values.
Shows dependency injection through function-based service factories and test doubles.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples, not a runnable library or package.
Examples assume TypeScript and Node.js service conventions.
Does not benchmark performance or compare functional programming libraries.
Requires adaptation to your domain types, error model, and testing framework.

use_cases.title: Refactor Service Logic
use_cases.description: Separate business rules from I/O so service behavior is easier to test and review.

use_cases.title: Teach Testable TypeScript
use_cases.description: Use concise examples to explain pure functions, immutability, and composition to a team.

use_cases.title: Design Error Handling
use_cases.description: Model recoverable failures with Result and Option patterns instead of hidden exceptions.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the pure core, impure shell pattern for a TypeScript service. Include when to use it and common mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript function and suggest a functional refactor using pure functions and immutable updates: [paste function].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Result Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Result-based pipeline for this request flow. Show validation, processing, formatting, and typed error boundaries: [describe flow].

prompt_templates.title: Review a Service Boundary
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Node.js service boundary for side effects, dependency injection, testability, and functional composition opportunities: [paste summary].

output_examples.input: Review a checkout service that mixes validation, database writes, and notification calls.
output: Validation and price calculations should move into pure functions.
Database writes and notifications should stay in a thin impure shell.
Inject repositories and notification clients so tests can use fakes.

output_examples.input: Help design typed error handling for an import job.
output: Use Result for validation and processing failures.
Use Option for optional lookup results that are not errors.
Map each failure into a domain error before returning from the workflow.

output_examples.input: Teach immutable updates to a TypeScript team.
output: Show object spread for shallow updates.
Use array map, filter, and spread instead of mutation.
Mark shared data as readonly where it improves safety.

best_practices: Separate pure business rules from I/O before adding new abstractions.
Use immutable updates when transforming shared domain objects.
Model recoverable errors with Result or Option when callers must handle them.
anti_patterns: Hiding database or network calls inside functions expected to be pure.
Mutating request or domain objects in shared service code.
Adding functional abstractions that obscure simple logic.

faq.question: Does this skill install a functional programming library?
faq.answer: No. It provides TypeScript patterns and examples that can be adapted to your codebase.

faq.question: Is it only useful for advanced functional programmers?
faq.answer: No. It starts with practical patterns such as pure functions, immutable updates, and dependency injection.

faq.question: Can it help with testing?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance focuses on reducing side effects and injecting dependencies so tests can use predictable inputs and fakes.

faq.question: Does it replace framework-specific architecture guidance?
faq.answer: No. It complements framework guidance by improving service logic, boundaries, and error handling.

faq.question: Can I use these patterns in existing Node.js code?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples are designed for incremental refactoring of TypeScript and Node.js services.

faq.question: Does it make every function pure?
faq.answer: No. It separates pure business logic from necessary I/O so each part has a clear role.
